root_idea.summary: The root centers on weakness or lack of solidity, expressed in speech as unseriousness and in the body as leanness.
root_idea.development: The evidence presents two related lexical branches: هَزْل as frivolous or unproductive speech, and هُزَال as loss of bodily fullness; the former is metaphorically likened to the latter.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under its normalized lexical citation form.

senses.definition: Frivolity or unserious, empty speech lacking substantial result or purpose.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression بِالْهَزْلِ, the term is negated and contrasts with serious, substantial discourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To jest, joke, or behave without earnestness; to be unserious in speech or in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of speech or conduct that is contrary to earnestness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leanness, meagreness, or emaciation; the opposite of fatness.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: هَزْلَى is cited as its plural form.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the noun's contrast with earnestness and the Form I verb's joking or unseriousness.
Defines the Form III verb as jesting or joking.
